messages.author: 4e81646001028f14
messages.subject: Sample size -> AICc
parts:
Dear Nick,

In your 2014 paper (Model selection in historical biogeography...) table 5 you presented AIC and AICc (which needs sample size).
 
What is sample size in the context of DEC?
number of terminals? number of areas?

Thank you in advance,

Peter

messages.author: 0e713d20fc7459b5
messages.subject: Re: Sample size -> AICc
parts:
Hi,

The Psychotria example uses the number of tip from the phylogeny:
samplesize = length(tr$tip.label)

HTH,
Torsten

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: Sample size -> AICc
parts:
Yep, sample size should be the number of tips in the tree.  Another, non-phylogenetic, model would be to draw the ranges randomly from a hat, and again the sample size would be the number of ranges you've observed.  We just typically use phylogenetic models because we think evolution has something to do with explaining our data  ;-).
Cheers,
Nick
